title: The Nuclear Age and the Cold War
summary: The rivalry between the USA and the USSR after 1945, capitalism versus communism, the arms race, the Berlin Wall, the Cuban Missile Crisis, the Cold War in Africa and its end.

notes.text: After World War II, the two **superpowers**, the **USA** and the **USSR** (Soviet Union), became bitter rivals. From about **1945 to 1991** they competed for power and influence around the world. It was called a **Cold War** because they never fought each other directly; instead they used threats, propaganda, an arms race, spying and **proxy wars** (wars fought by their allies).

notes.caption: Two opposing systems
rows: Private ownership of businesses; free market; profits for owners
The state owns land, factories and businesses; the government plans the economy
One party (the Communist Party); no free elections
Freedom of speech, press and religion emphasised
Strict control and censorship; secret police

notes.text: The nuclear age and the arms race

The USA used atomic bombs in 1945. In **1949** the USSR tested its own. Both sides then built thousands of nuclear weapons, including hydrogen bombs and long-range missiles. This **arms race** led to the idea of **MAD (Mutually Assured Destruction)**: if one side attacked, the other would strike back and both would be destroyed, so neither dared to start a nuclear war.

The two powers also competed in the **space race**: the USSR launched **Sputnik**, the first satellite, in 1957 and sent Yuri Gagarin into space in 1961; the USA landed Neil Armstrong on the moon in **1969**.

rows: Germany and Berlin were split; West Germany allied with the USA, East Germany with the USSR
The USSR blocked roads into West Berlin; the Western allies flew in supplies for almost a year
Communist North Korea (supported by the USSR and China) against South Korea (supported by the USA and UN)
East Germany built a wall to stop its people escaping to the West

The USSR placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, close to the USA. After 13 tense days, Khrushchev agreed to remove them, and the USA secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey. The world came close to nuclear war
The USA fought to stop communist North Vietnam taking over South Vietnam, but withdrew; Vietnam was united under communism

notes.text: Both superpowers supported governments and movements in newly independent African countries. In **Angola** (from 1975), the MPLA government was supported by the USSR and Cuban troops, while UNITA was supported by the USA and apartheid South Africa. The battle of **Cuito Cuanavale** (1987–1988) led to talks that brought **Namibia's independence** in 1990.

notes.label: Link to South Africa
notes.text: The apartheid government claimed it was protecting South Africa from communism (the *swart gevaar* and *rooi gevaar*: 'black danger' and 'red danger') and used this to win support from Western countries. When the Cold War ended, this argument lost its power, which helped bring about the negotiations of 1990.
The end of the Cold War

items: From 1985 the Soviet leader **Mikhail Gorbachev** introduced *glasnost* (openness) and *perestroika* (economic restructuring).
The USA and USSR signed treaties to reduce nuclear weapons.
Communist governments in Eastern Europe collapsed in 1989. On **9 November 1989** the **Berlin Wall** was opened, and Germany reunited in 1990.
In **December 1991** the USSR broke up into 15 independent countries, including Russia and Ukraine.
